delivery.outcome: A first-time target can prove and atomically account for newly installed managed standard files without exempting overwritten target-owned content
nonGoals: No change to Docker defaults or workstream ownership
No adoption payload, dependency, version or release change
No downstream mutation, push, pull request, merge or publication

architecture.decision: Represent initial adoption with a null base revision and exempt only hash-verified managed targets absent from the accepted Git base
interfaceChanges: delivery.standardAdoption.fromRevision accepts null to declare initial adoption
architecture.rollback: Use the existing two-SHA upgrade-only declaration; initial adopters receive no managed-path exemption

validation.evidence: Schema and direct parser assertions accept null bootstrap and preserve two-SHA upgrade
Bootstrap fixture binds an absent base package/lock to the complete head lock and managed hashes
A pre-existing managed target remains inside ticket scope while new managed targets are exempt

commands: all commands from the Linux CI test job
validation.evidence: Existing upgrade mutations and the full standard contract pass
